steps.content: Carrying Hestia on your back, you tread through the darkness. The bells on her jingle, the sound much softer now.
Under her guidance, you find a safe place to rest. The fire provides you with light, warmth, and protection. Since entering the mutated area, you've never felt so at ease.
Hestia sits beside you. She may be tired or still nervous, as she's placed her torch beside her and is hugging her knees quietly.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Not anymore, we won.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I just didn't expect... that such a terrifying monster could be defeated by us two kids. I'd been so scared for so long only for it to turn out this easy...
You smile. After all, that monster was a projection of her fear. As long as she herself faced up to it, of course it was nothing more than a paper tiger.
But you decide against giving her this lecture.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Of course, you are the great priestess.

steps.content: Her face turns red again, poking in your direction with the tail end of her torch.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Stop mocking me! I know you don't believe what I say!
But her angry poke misses. You can't help but laugh out loud.
The smile disappears from the girl's face. She withdraws her torch feebly, her voice becoming somewhat downcast.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I... I guess you all know that I'm no priestess.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: If the Pyromater's oracles were real, the world wouldn't have ended up like this...
You watch her quietly. Under the firelight, the girl's eyes reflect a dim color, as if looking into a distant past.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I've mentioned Stor Town before, right? That place... is sort of my hometown. It's a rundown small town in a desert.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: It's not far from here and has suffered many disasters. Folks in that shabby place don't know much about the world. Even in that sorry state, all they knew was to beg for the Pyromater's mercy instead of getting out. In the end, only around four hundred people survived with "her blessings."

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...My whole family died too. I was the only one left. A frail, nearly blind kid who'd had no education whatsoever. I wasn't able to snatch even just a few bites of food. Nothing but death awaited me.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: But I didn't want to die. If those stupid fire believers could live, why should I have to die... So I told them that these eyes weren't blind but meant to reflect the form of God. That I didn't see demons in my dreams every night, but divine oracles bestowed upon me by God.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Of course they did. I'm timid and sensitive enough to sense those things. These eyes can't see the normal world, but the bad and ominous stuff? Never miss it.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Besides, I'm smart enough. Whatever kind of <color=#fb9259>priestess</color> they wanted, I could play along. Those folks suffering out there were dying for a god to protect them.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Those stubborn scholars from the expedition were the only people who cared to ask all those questions, and then there's you...
Another poke from the torch, this time gentler, just enough to express her annoyance.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...It wasn't all lies, though. I did predict a few disasters and save Stor Town from hell more than once.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: In return, I only asked for food and protection, plus a bit of respect... It's a fair trade, isn't it?
She says slightly sheepishly, shrinking a little as if fearing your judgment.

steps.speaker: Option
options: You've made the best out of your situation.
...Having to lie constantly must be exhausting.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Life's tough out there. It's already an achievement for a kid at your age to survive...

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Hmph, you're a kid too, only with better luck. Of course, I know I'm awesome.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Ha... These days, people are ready to kill to survive. Deceiving others isn't that hard for a kid who has nothing. I can do it for the rest of my life.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: But... I still ended up here at last.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't you the revered priestess? Why would Stor Town and your believers let you go?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Let me go? Haha, they sent me here.
She laughs, her voice becoming cold.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I did predict a few disasters and saved the townsfolk a few times, but the luck of a blind little liar would eventually run out at some point.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I got really anxious and worried that time and told them to leave quickly if they wanted to live. There was only so much I could do, but back then, I truly hoped they could live.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Heh... How stupid. The priestess was supposed to wield divine power to save her believers. How could she leave them to fend for themselves?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: The mayor said since I had proven my power, I could definitely save everyone... So they tied me up and brought me here.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: No matter how I pleaded and apologized, they wouldn't listen. My "believers" tied me up, kicked me out of the vehicle, then prayed in the direction where the "mighty god descended", saying that...

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Stor Town sent the most devout <color=#fb9259>Priestess of Fire</color>, who would nourish the flames with her own power and life, all to appease the <color=#fb9259>god</color>'s anger.
You freeze, clenching your fists involuntarily.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Haha... You're not angry, are you? Don't be mad, they've already received their punishment.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: How would sacrificing a fake priestess stop the disaster? If God really existed, it would only anger them! How could they be so dumb?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Haha, maybe their god has already unleashed their fury and blown up that shabby town? Serves them right!
She laughs unnaturally, her body convulsing. She doesn't look like a child of her age at all and even seems a little hysterical. It only makes you sad.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You left Stor Town and escaped from the Pyromater Sect. What you found here wasn't any god...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But that expedition you like.
She still staring into the void, yet her gaze softens.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Just a bunch of fools. They're even more gullible than the folks in Stor Town.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: When they first found me, I was on edge all the time. To survive, I had to cling to this sliver of hope. I made up so many lies, tried to be helpful, and said nice things, all because I was afraid they'd abandon me too and leave me to die.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: But they never wanted anything from me, never asked me to prove myself or be useful... They were indeed quite careless, taking in a kid full of lies emerging out of nowhere like that.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: It's really dangerous here and resources are more than scarce, yet they were willing to spare their medicine on me, share their food, and waste bullets to protect me. Even though they didn't believe in my made-up god, they never exposed me either.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Where did they get the courage? Did they really think they could survive? That they could save me, save everyone, save the whole world?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...What a bunch of fools.
The girl's voice dwindles.

steps.speaker: Option
options: You seem to really like those fools.

steps.content: She doesn't respond, and after a long while, she nods slightly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why did you split up? You're alone here.
Hestia doesn't answer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you run into danger and get separated?
Still, no response.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hestia, what happened? Tell me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This path is too dark and bumpy to walk alone, but now we're together. I'll help you find them.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...No. It was me... I ran away from you guys.
Silence. For a long moment, all you can hear is her low breathing.
After a while, she begins softly.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>The Perishing Star sinks into the abyss. The abyss connects to the dream. The dream brings back echoes. The echoes tell you to follow the moonlight and reach the stars...</color>

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: That day you told everyone that, saying if we set off when the moon rose, we could make it out of the maze and find the real path.
Her grip on the torch tightens and she curls up, muttering to herself as if entranced.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: How happy they were... Collecting data, calculating the moon phase, and conducting experiments, thinking they could finally escape the temporal loop and uncover the truth behind the Perishing Star and the disasters.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: But only I saw it... At the end of the path, at the edge of the dead city, under the Illusory Moon, lay an indescribable source. The truth you wanted to witness was absolutely unbearable. The redemption you sought would only hasten the end.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: If only you'd blurted out some gibberish as I would... to stop them from going on that journey with no return, from approaching that twisted, disgusting... that thing...

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: It's... the real god...
Illusory Moon, Perishing Star, dead city, source? Under the guide's direction, did the expedition take action? Where did they go? Did this really happen, or is this also part of the trap?

Regardless, you've never been closer to the past. Hestia's hollow gaze is fixed in one direction. Following her gaze, you see only darkness, but you're certain something else lies beyond that. You grab her hand eagerly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did they go there? That way? Can we still catch up with them now?
She jerks awake, but also seems suddenly irritated. Hestia shakes off your hand.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I've told you not to go. Will you ever listen to me?!
Taken aback, you realize it's too late to try to calm her now. She gets riled up.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I've said it so many times. Don't go, you'll die. Why won't you listen? Even if I used to lie for a living, sometimes I do tell the truth. Why can't you trust me just once?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Have you forgotten all the trouble we've gotten into just because you must wander around and do your investigation? You never listen. And they're just like you. They insisted on going. What could I do?

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I could only run! Was I supposed to just die with you? I'm not part of the expedition anyway. I don't share your great purpose!

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I'm not some great scholar or brave guide. I've never been to school. I don't have any noble ambition or courage. I'm constantly scared by my own nightmares. I can't understand your ideals or find the same motivation.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: All I've ever done is try to survive. I tell whatever lie I must tell and use whoever I must use. I'm just a selfish, useless, blind parasite. A liar who's abandoned those who have helped me.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I was never part of the expedition, just a coward. Every step I've taken following you guys has been exhausting...

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I really... can't go on anymore...
Unable to say another word, she bows her head deeply, leaning against the torch. The young guide who's been staring into darkness her whole life is already broken in body and spirit.
You finally make a decision.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Huh?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's not go to look for the expedition. We'll turn around. I'll take you away from here, to a truly safe place, away from all dangers. A place where you can finally live at ease.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: But what about them...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They told me to come and get you. They gave me these powerful red spikes so I can protect you.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: You're lying.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But if they knew I was here, they would say the same thing. They would want me to take you away.
Hestia freezes. You hesitate for a moment, but finally take her hand and gently embrace this girl who's been hurt countless times.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The world is cruel enough. Even those adults in Stor Town didn't find the courage to face the disaster and pushed a child like you into the fire...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So, you shouldn't feel ashamed of your fear. The expedition would never look down on you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They refused to leave you behind because of their principle. They let you go because they heeded your warning. They knew the path ahead was dangerous, so they wanted to keep you out of it.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: Then why did they still go...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Probably to look for a better world... A world where children worry about nothing and aren't forced to be brave in a place like this. A world where adults protect children and allow them to grow up safely.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You know, that's just the kind of people they are.
Although she doesn't answer, you feel her nod slightly in your arms. She's gradually calmed down.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Besides, you're in fact incredibly brave. A real coward would either hide at the camp or run far away, yet you've come to this place and set up this magic circle, waiting for them to return in the dark despite being terrified.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I hadn't come, you would have already gone after them, right?
Hestia flushes again. It seems you're right.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...I don't know. I'm not that brave. Even if I really went to find you guys, it would be because...

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: I no longer have the courage to be alone...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I think "too scared to be alone" and "wanting to return to your important ones" mean the same thing to you now.
Her body trembles slightly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But we're just kids now. We're not strong enough to protect ourselves. If we died recklessly on the way, it would only bring them more sorrow.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's not a kid's job to save the world. We just need to grow up properly so we can follow them on the same path later.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Hmm.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's go back. Before coming to find you, I've already figured out the exit. Once we're out, we'll immediately go find capable adults to rescue the expedition.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've been scared for too long on this journey. From now on, I'll protect you. I hope you won't be tormented by fear anymore.
She nudges you, wiping the tears from her face, crying and laughing at the same time.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: ...Stop trying to sound like an adult.

steps.speaker: Hestia
steps.content: You're even younger than me. How come you never seem scared?
Saying nothing to her half-joking question, you simply take her hand and keep walking, glad that she can't see your expression right now.
